#178 @user_110: Perhaps it’s just me, but that post reads like ai.

#179 @user_119: user_110: that post reads like ai. Probably machine-translated from Chinese.

#180 @user_109: Written in Chinese and have translated to English by AI. Not perfect but understandable.

#181 @user_107: One aspect that I have not read in this thread (I may have missed it) relates to child safety. Button cell batteries can cause the death of a child if swallowed as they can get stuck and burn through the gut. As someone with small grandchildren I aim to have as few button cells in the house as possible. Here in Australia button cells are packaged to be child-resistant, but it is so easy to drop and loose a small battery when replacing one in a hearing aid.

#182 @user_117: The type of cell used in disposable battery hearing aids doesn’t present the burn risk, just choke. WH

#183 @user_107: Surely the type of battery chemistry is irrelevant. It is the electrical discharge caused by saliva contact that does the damage. See: Button batteries guide | ACCC Product Safety
